patterns_data.top_pattern: Authorization coding and facility mapping issues are inflating apparent spend
patterns_data.what_is_impacting: Authorization coding and facility mapping in CA / NY / CO
patterns_data.pattern_details: A meaningful share of the reported increase is tied to authorization-code movement and facility records landing in unmapped buckets, so this is a gating validation issue before any policy or provider action. CA drives the largest auth-code shift, NY shows the same pattern, and CO plus CA also show spend flowing through Not Mapped facility classifications. The business risk is acting on what may be data movement rather than real utilization or reimbursement change.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: If this is not cleaned up first, downstream UM, reimbursement, and network actions may target the wrong drivers.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a joint UM operations and data-quality reconciliation on PA-required coding and facility mapping for CA, NY, and CO, then restate the impacted segments before changing policy or provider strategy.
patterns_data.validation_reason: Both auth-code distribution shifts and unmapped facility buckets are explicitly flagged as requiring validation before action.
evidence_summary: CA authorization-code distribution accounts for +$3.4M and is flagged for validation before action.
NY shows another +$0.7M from authorization-code distribution shifts.
CO PPO Not Mapped facility spend adds +$0.6M on 17 more admissions while paid per admit fell, pointing to classification movement rather than price.
CA Not Mapped facility buckets add about +$0.6M across HMO and PPO, concentrated at UC IRVINE MEDICAL CENTER.

patterns_data.pattern_details: CA has a highly concentrated catastrophic-case pattern rather than broad-based inpatient inflation. Two ungroupable case clusters make up most of the impact, with additional isolated high-cost bowel, chest, infection, kidney, and circulatory cases spread across a few providers. This should be treated as a case-level outlier and classification review, not as a systemwide utilization trend.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: A few extreme admissions can materially distort trend and require different action than broad utilization management.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Perform claim-level clinical and coding validation on these CA outlier admissions, confirm grouping accuracy, and route validated cases for individual case management review.

The remaining increase is fragmented across isolated bowel, chest, infection, kidney, and circulatory cases.
Provider concentration appears at UC IRVINE MEDICAL CENTER, LOMPOC VALLEY MEDICAL CENTER, and CROUSE HEALTH HOSPITAL, but all on very small counts.

patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Route GA, VA, and WI to a post-acute management review covering LTCH admission criteria, discharge planning to lower-cost settings, and LTCH/rehab contract terms.
evidence_summary: GA POS LTCH is primarily unit-cost driven at +$2.5M with no admission growth and about +$1.3M paid per admit.
VA LTCH adds +$1.1M in POS and +$0.4M in PPO, with roughly +$180K paid per admit on small counts.
WI clinical aftercare cases add +$2.4M, led by circulatory aftercare and spinal cord injury aftercare.
WI physical rehab adds +$0.3M with 4 more admissions and about +$82K paid per admit.

patterns_data.pattern_details: CO shows a provider-economics pattern across multiple facility types rather than a single clinical spike. patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Run a CO network financial review of acute and children's reimbursement terms and pair it with UM review of rehab and EPO acute admissions to identify avoidable high-cost placements.
evidence_summary: CO EPO acute hospital added +$1.4M with 2 more admissions and about +$16K paid per admit even as claim count fell.
CO PPO children's facility added +$1.0M despite 7 fewer admissions, indicating clear unit-cost pressure.
CO PPO acute hospital added +$0.8M even with 24 fewer admissions, again pointing to reimbursement rather than utilization.
CO PPO physical rehab added +$0.3M on 8 more admissions with about +$28K paid per admit.

patterns_data.pattern_details: This is a distinct catastrophic-case pattern driven by a handful of transplant, heart assist, cardiac, and other severe inpatient events. The spend is concentrated in very small counts, with one large unattributed exposure and a few isolated provider-level cases making up most of the change. Business action should stay at case level and begin with attribution and claim validation before broader policy conclusions are drawn.
patterns_data.why_it_matters: Catastrophic outliers can distort trend quickly, but the right response is case-level validation and management rather than broad market changes.
patterns_data.recommended_next_step: Validate attribution and coding on these rare cases first, then route confirmed cases for individual clinical outlier review and high-cost case management.
patterns_data.validation_reason: The pattern is concentrated in very small numbers and includes UNATTRIBUTED exposure, making claim attribution and grouping validation necessary before broader action.
evidence_summary: Heart transplant and heart assist activity accounts for most of the increase, including a coronary artery dissection case at +$1.5M and a heart assist system implant case at +$0.5M.
Additional isolated neurologic, gastrointestinal, HIV/pneumonia, and postpartum infection cases contribute the remaining increase.
The pattern is flagged for low baseline and small numbers, with exposure also appearing in UNATTRIBUTED records.
